verdict: CoStar grew revenue 14% to a record $952M and swung back to a $74M profit as it reined in the marketing spend that dragged it to a loss a year ago.

kpis.label: Revenue
kpis.note: +14% YoY, vs $834M a year ago — a record quarter

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP diluted)
kpis.note: vs a $0.07 loss per share a year ago; adjusted EPS was $0.38

kpis.label: Adjusted EBITDA
kpis.note: Doubled YoY and the highest ever — earnings before interest, tax, writedowns and stock pay, on the company's adjusted basis

kpis.label: Residential revenue
kpis.note: +23% YoY — Apartments.com, Homes.com and other home marketplaces, now almost half of all revenue

segments.name: CoStar
segments.note: Subscriptions to the flagship commercial real estate database — property data, analytics and news for brokers, lenders and owners. Up 8%.

segments.name: LoopNet
segments.note: The marketplace for commercial property for sale and for lease. Up 13%.

segments.name: Other Commercial Real Estate
segments.note: Other commercial real estate products and marketplaces. Down 8% vs a year ago.

segments.name: Residential Real Estate
segments.note: Home and apartment marketplaces, including Apartments.com, Homes.com and Domain in Australia. Up 23% — the fastest-growing part of the group.

opex.name: Selling and marketing
opex.note: Sales teams, commissions and marketing for sites like Apartments.com and Homes.com. Down from $418M a year ago as the company cut spend after its big residential investment push.

opex.name: Software development
opex.note: Building and improving the websites, apps and data platforms. Up slightly from $106M a year ago.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: Running the company — finance, legal and admin. Down from $157M a year ago as cost savings kicked in.

opex.name: Customer base amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of customer lists and relationships bought in acquisitions over their useful lives. Up from $32M a year ago after recent deals.

takeaways.title: Record revenue, led by residential
takeaways.text: Revenue reached a record $952M, up 14%. Residential Real Estate jumped 23% to $460M, CoStar rose 8% to $344M and LoopNet rose 13% to $89M, while Other Commercial Real Estate fell 8% to $59M. Net new bookings were $37M in the quarter.

takeaways.title: Profitability surged as spend was reined in
takeaways.text: Adjusted EBITDA doubled to $229M, the highest ever. Selling and marketing fell to $366M from $418M a year ago even as revenue grew, and total operating expenses fell to $657M from $713M. Management put this year's cost savings at about $150M and raised full-year Adjusted EBITDA guidance to $820M-$840M.

takeaways.title: Back in profit after last year's loss
takeaways.text: Net income was $74M, or $0.18 per diluted share, vs a $31M loss a year ago — a $105M swing. Operating income was $84M vs a $51M loss, and the Residential segment's EBITDA turned positive at $16M, vs a $101M loss a year ago, as the heavy Homes.com investment phase eased.

oneTimers: Operating costs include $15M of acquisition and integration-related costs (the Zonda acquisition closed in August 2026) and $3M of settlements and impairments that the company excludes from Adjusted EBITDA and Adjusted Net Income.
footerNote: As reported in $M; the lines tie exactly. Interest expense, net ($1M) and other income, net ($1M) offset, so there is no other-income line.
follow100Note: The revenue split is the disaggregated revenue by product in the release and the Form 10-Q revenue note; CoStar reports two operating segments, Commercial Real Estate ($492M) and Residential Real Estate ($460M).
